USA.head: 48% of new US capacity arrives with its own power station
USA.note: Of ~17 GW under construction, 36% is behind-the-meter and 12% is a utility building dedicated plant; the other 52% draws on the ordinary grid. The dedicated half is weighted three parts on-site engines and simple-cycle turbines (~550 g) to one part combined-cycle (~375 g). Observed construction, not a mandate — the best-evidenced entry here.
USA.src: ITK Research / CBRE / JLL construction split; Global Energy Monitor gas pipeline

CHN.head: New Chinese data centres must source 80% renewables
CHN.note: China builds no dedicated generation for data centres — they draw on abundant provincial grids. But a 2025 policy requires all new data centres to obtain 80% of their electricity from renewables. If enforced as physical supply rather than certificates, new Chinese load is far cleaner than the Chinese grid average.
CHN.src: Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, Feb 2026

IRL.head: Generation matching import capacity, 80% from additional renewables
IRL.note: The hardest requirement anywhere: a new Irish data centre must provide generation or storage matching the maximum import capacity it requests, and take at least 80% of annual demand from additional Irish renewable projects. Already-contracted PPAs do not count.

SGP.head: New allocations must be at least 50% green
SGP.note: Singapore allocates data centre capacity by application. DC-CFA2 requires at least 50% green energy — biomethane, low-carbon ammonia, hydrogen, fuel cells with capture, or on-site solar — plus PUE below 1.3.
